Charge-off-only records share the same delinquency anchor (COLLECTION/CHARGE-OFF context) and are included.

adapters.citation: Consumer Credit Reporting Agencies Act (California), Civ. Code § 1785.13(a)(8)
adapters.limb: any other adverse information that antedates the report by more than seven years
adapters.start_record: the recorded start is 'the date of the adverse item' under § 1785.13(a)(8) (any other adverse information), with § 1785.13(b) moving the seven-year period (for paragraphs (5) and (8)) 180 days after the delinquency commencement 'with respect to any account that is placed for collection (internally or by referral to a third party, whichever is earlier), charged to profit and loss, or subjected to any similar action'. The supported event-date timing (rating's own date, NO 180-day offset) is NOT yet established: absence of COLLECTION/CHARGE-OFF wording does not establish that (b) is inapplicable because (b) also covers 'any similar action'. Collection/charge-off accounts are governed by the (a)(5) collection branch (US-CA-CCRAA-1785-13-A-5-COLLECTION-7Y, anchor_day_offset: 180).

finding_disabled.reason: OWNER-CANDIDATE-007 correction (2026-10-04): the supported event-date timing branch is NOT established. Absence of COLLECTION/CHARGE-OFF wording does not establish that § 1785.13(b) is inapplicable, because (b) also applies to 'any similar action'. This adapter is fail closed (finding_allowed: false) until an admitted evidence basis establishes event-date applicability or supplies the (b) delinquency-based timing.
finding_disabled.enabling_evidence_required: an admitted report-evidenced account/action context with source provenance that positively establishes the account was NOT placed for collection, charged off, or subjected to a similar action — or the delinquency commencement required by (b) for a collection/charge-off/similar account.

adapters.applicability_note: tri-state account/action context, resolved PER RECORD with source provenance. (1) ESTABLISHED (b) CONTEXT — the record prints COLLECTION / CHARGE-OFF / PLACED FOR COLLECTION (reportedAccount.accountActionContext = COLLECTION_OR_CHARGE_OFF) — is NOT_APPLICABLE here: the (a)(5) collection branch governs with delinquency-based timing and the 180-day offset. (2) ESTABLISHED SUPPORTED EVENT-DATE CONTEXT is APPLICABLE (event-date timing, no 180-day offset), but NO admitted evidence basis produces this state yet, so it is unreachable until such evidence is admitted. (3) UNKNOWN / CONFLICTING / UNSUPPORTED context — including an unlabelled 'similar action' (repossession, foreclosure, write-off) whose legal meaning this build does NOT assign — is APPLICABILITY_UNRESOLVED and emits NO finding.

exceptions.basis: Civ. Code § 1785.13(a)(8) — seven years from the date of the adverse information; the official text records no exception (the § 1785.13(d) ten-year outer limit is a separate rule, CRP-LSRC-0269, not an exception to (a)(8))

adapters.source_retrieval_note: OWNER-CANDIDATE-007 (B, 2026-10-04): the period and the (b) applicability are recorded from the official California legislature text (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov, Civ. Code § 1785.13(a)(8)+(b), Stats. 2024 Ch. 520 SB 1061): '(8) Any other adverse information that antedates the report by more than seven years.' and '(b) The seven-year period specified in paragraphs (5) and (8) ... with respect to any account that is placed for collection ..., charged to profit and loss, or subjected to any similar action, upon the expiration of the 180-day period ...'. Because (b) applies to (8) only for collection/charge-off/similar accounts, this residual branch applies the rating's own date with NO 180-day offset and defers collection/charge-off accounts to the (a)(5) branch; the offset is never invented here. The corpus maps (a)(8) to CRP-LSRC-0268 (legalCorpus/rules.ca.ts, 7DDBF5C4).

anchor_evidence.why_this_is_the_recorded_start: s.4(b) runs from the later of the last payment and the date the debt was incurred. The incurred date is not printed, and an account-opening or first-delinquency date is NOT substituted for it. For a debt incurred once, the last payment date is the later of the two; for a REVOLVING account the outstanding balance may include amounts charged after the last payment, so the incurred date can be later and is then UNKNOWN - which is stated in the consumer wording rather than assumed away.
anchor_evidence.ambiguity_rule: the anchor is the record own printed Last Payment Date; a label with no value, or a value that cannot be read to a precise date, produces no anchor and is never measured from a neighbouring record
